  "text": "The baby monitor began picking up my mother's voice six months after her funeral.

“She's cold,” it said.

Upstairs, our daughter had kicked off her blanket.

My husband blamed interference. I asked him what frequency dead women used.

We bought another monitor.

“Not that bottle,” my mother said the following evening.

The glass cracked as I lifted it from the warmer.

After that, I kept the receiver beside me.

She warned us about a loose crib screw, a fever, a wasp beneath the changing table. Sometimes she sang the song she'd sung when I was small, including the verse she'd invented about our dog.

I began saying goodnight to her.

One evening, she answered.

“Goodnight, sweetheart.”

I cried so hard my husband unplugged the monitor.

It kept singing.

We moved our daughter into our room. The receiver stayed in the kitchen, wrapped in a towel.

At midnight, my mother's voice came through clearly.

“You can't keep her in there forever.”

My husband took a hammer to it.

For a week, the house was quiet.

Then our daughter said her first word.

“Cold.”

She was looking at the empty corner behind my chair.

I called my sister. I hadn't told her anything about the monitor, but I asked whether she remembered the extra verse about the dog.

“Mom didn't make that up,” she said. “You did. You used to sing it to that corner in your bedroom.”

Behind me, my daughter laughed.

My sister went quiet when I told her.

“Listen,” she said finally. “When she starts talking properly, don't let her tell it her name.”"
